title: VoltPilot v2 Edge Desired / Arbitration Payloads
description: The v2 LOCAL-BUS contract between the flow runtime (compiled user flows running in the Node-RED layer) and the Go core's arbitration: a flow's action node publishes a DESIRED value ('Wunsch') on edge/entities/{entity_id}/desired; the core arbitrates competing desires per entity, clamps the winner through the per-entity guard chain, and reports every decision on edge/entities/{entity_id}/arbitration. Flows NEVER write registers and NEVER publish actuation topics - the core alone publishes the guard-clamped command to the driver layer (see edge-desired-arbitration.md for the full topic family). This is a BINDING contract; unlike the versionless v1 local-bus namespace (edge-app/core/internal/localbus/localbus.go), the v2 entity topics are contract-grade because user-authored logic runs against them. schema_version is per-contract and starts at 1.0 (a brand-new contract, no predecessor).

x-topics.desired: edge/entities/{entity_id}/desired  (flow runtime -> core, QoS1, NOT retained - desires expire via ttl_s, a retained stale desire would be a command from the past)
x-topics.arbitration: edge/entities/{entity_id}/arbitration  (core -> observers, QoS1, NOT retained - event stream; the latest state is also in the core's state snapshot / :8484 API and summarized in the cloud status heartbeat)

x-semantics.ownership: At any instant at most ONE desired holds an entity (the holder). Selection: highest priority class wins; within the same class the current holder keeps the entity until its TTL lapses or it releases - a same-class challenger is rejected with reason 'arbitration:conflict' (no last-writer-wins, no oscillation). Cross-flow same-class conflicts are already refused at flow activation time (flow-graph exclusive-resource validation); the runtime rule is the backstop.
x-semantics.priority: Classes rank safety > grid > contract > market > flow. On the current edge, safety/grid/contract do not appear as desires at all - they are the guard-chain clamps applied to WHATEVER wins (restrict-only, never bypassable). The classes are reserved in this schema for the E8 command-arbitration masters (Netzbetreiber via EEBUS = grid, Direktvermarkter = contract). The core's plan executor injects the cloud plan slots as class 'market'. Flow-sourced desires are ALWAYS class 'flow' - the core rejects a flow desired claiming any other class (reason 'arbitration:priority_not_allowed').
x-semantics.override: override=true on a class-'flow' desired elevates it above 'market' (never above contract/grid/safety) for its bounded TTL (max 14400 s). This is the deliberate 'boost' escape hatch: explicit owner intent may cost money ('kann nerven'), never compliance. Arbitration events flag the elevation loudly; the plan re-takes the entity on expiry.
x-semantics.ttl: ttl_s is REQUIRED - there are no immortal desires. On expiry the entity falls to the next-highest active desired, else to the entity's failsafe behavior declared in its registry config (edge/entities/{entity_id}/config), never to a remembered stale value. Flows are expected to re-emit standing desires on their triggers (interval trigger recommended; keep ttl_s comfortably above the re-emit period).
x-semantics.guards: Arbitration selects; guards decide. The winning desired is clamped through the per-entity guard chain (v1 order, verified in edge-app/core/internal/guards/guards.go: rated band -> SoC window -> EEG solar-only charge -> observed grid-limit envelope -> band again; peak-shave after all compliance clamps, restrict-only). granted reports the post-guard value; outcome 'clamped' when granted != requested.
x-semantics.identity: The entity_id in the payload MUST equal the {entity_id} topic segment; the core ignores mismatches (the v1 topic==payload identity rule).

entity_id.description: Entity id from the entity registry. MQTT-topic-safe by construction (the provisioning ref pattern); UUIDs recommended (the cloud registry row id).

priority.description: Priority class. Rank order safety(100) > grid(90, Netzbetreiber) > contract(80, Direktvermarkter) > market(60, cloud plan) > flow(40, user flows). See x-semantics.priority for what may claim which class.

command.description: One command from the generic v2 vocabulary. Sign conventions are fixed per capability, not per command: storage setpoint_kw + = charge / - = discharge (the v1 battery_setpoint_kw convention); consumer setpoint_kw + = consume; generators are never commanded to produce - only capped via limit_kw/limit_pct (the v1 pv_limit_kw safety posture: a limit only ever REDUCES generation).

source.description: Who emitted the desired. kind 'flow' = a compiled user/vendor flow (flow identity required, stamped by the compiler into the action node - not customer-editable); 'plan-executor' = the core's own market-class injection of the active plan slot; 'cloud-command' = a cloud-sent ad-hoc command (E12 portfolio runner / E8 masters); 'local-ui' = the :8484 operator surface.

source_ref.description: Compact reference to a desired in arbitration events.

request_id.description: Correlates this desired with its arbitration events. Unique per emission; re-emitting the same standing wish MAY reuse the id (refresh: same holder, TTL restarts).

override.description: Only meaningful on class 'flow': elevates this desired above 'market' for its TTL (never above contract/grid/safety). TTL is additionally capped at 14400 s when set. Default false.

ttl_s.description: Seconds this desired stays valid from issued_at. REQUIRED - no immortal desires. RECOMMENDED <= 900 with re-emission on a trigger; override desires are capped at 14400 by the arbiter.

issued_at.description: When the emitter produced this desired (RFC 3339, UTC). The arbiter anchors TTL at min(issued_at, receive time) - a future-dated desired gains nothing.

arbitration.title: edge/entities/{entity_id}/arbitration payload (event)
arbitration.description: One arbitration/guard decision event for one entity. Emitted on every state change: a desired accepted/clamped/rejected, a holder superseded or expired, a release, or the fall to the registry failsafe. 'holder' reports who owns the entity AFTER the event (null = no active desired, the entity runs its registry failsafe).

outcome.description: accepted = subject desired won, granted == requested. clamped = subject won but guards reduced it (granted != requested). rejected = subject refused (validation, capability, priority, conflict). superseded = subject lost the entity to a higher-priority desired. expired = subject's TTL lapsed. released = emitter withdrew (a desired with command absent semantics is not defined; release = TTL expiry or an explicit new desired from the same source with ttl_s honored - see .md). fallback = no active desired remains, entity runs its registry failsafe.

subject.description: The desired this event is about (absent only for outcome 'fallback' when triggered by e.g. plan staleness rather than a specific desired).

granted.description: The post-guard command actually forwarded to the driver layer as a result of this event; null when nothing is forwarded for the subject (rejected/superseded/expired) - the holder's granted value continues to apply.

reasons.description: Why, machine-readable, most significant first. Known stages (open set): arbitration:conflict, arbitration:priority, arbitration:priority_not_allowed, arbitration:ttl, arbitration:override, validation:schema, validation:identity, capability:unsupported_command, guard:rated_band, guard:soc_window, guard:solar_only_charge, guard:grid_limit_14a, guard:peak_shave, guard:limit_reduce_only.

holder.description: Who holds the entity after this event; null = registry failsafe active.
